# Fix It Notes

> Plain-English DIY home repair guides at https://homerepair.samcbarth.com. Answer-first DIY repair guides with tools, steps, safety notes and when to call a licensed pro. Sources are linked on every guide.

## Plumbing
- [How to Find and Shut Off Your Main Water Valve](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/shut-off-main-water/): The main shutoff is usually where the water line enters the house: in a basement or crawl space on the front wall, near the water heater, in a garage, or in a utility closet. Turn a round gate valve clockwise until it stops; turn a ball valve lever a quarter turn so it sits crosswise to the pipe.
- [How to Fix Low Water Pressure at a Faucet (Clean the Aerator)](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/clean-faucet-aerator/): If only one faucet has weak or sputtering flow, the aerator screen at the tip of the spout is probably clogged with sediment or mineral scale. Unscrew it, rinse and soak it in white vinegar, or replace it with a new aerator of the same size.
- [How to Fix a Leak Under the Sink (P-Trap and Drain)](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/fix-leaking-p-trap/): Dry everything, run water, and watch to find the exact drip. Leaks at the curved P-trap are usually fixed by reseating or replacing the slip-nut washers or swapping in a new plastic trap kit; leaks at the supply lines need a new braided connector.
- [How to Fix a Leaky Faucet](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/fix-leaky-faucet/): A dripping faucet usually has a worn cartridge, washer or O-ring. Shut off the water under the sink, remove the handle, pull the old cartridge or washer, and install an exact match from the faucet's manufacturer.
- [How to Fix a Running Toilet](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/fix-running-toilet/): A toilet that keeps running is almost always leaking past a worn flapper or overfilling through the overflow tube. Do a food-coloring dye test, adjust the chain or float, and replace the flapper or fill valve if adjusting does not stop it.
- [How to Unclog a Sink Drain Without Chemicals](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/unclog-sink-drain/): Start by pulling and cleaning the stopper, then plunge with the overflow blocked. If that fails, clean the P-trap under the sink or run a hand drain snake. Skip chemical drain cleaners; they rarely clear a full clog.
- [How to Unclog a Toilet](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/unclog-toilet/): Use a flange plunger with a tight seal and pull back as hard as you push, about a dozen strokes. If plunging fails, a closet auger (toilet auger) clears most stubborn clogs without scratching the bowl.
- [Water Heater Not Heating? What to Check First](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/water-heater-not-hot/): For an electric water heater, check the breaker first, then press the red high-limit reset behind the upper access panel with the power off. For gas, confirm the gas valve is open and the pilot is lit, following the lighting label on the tank. If a reset trips again or the pilot will not stay lit, call a licensed pro.

## Electrical
- [How to Replace a Light Switch](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/replace-light-switch/): Turn off the breaker, confirm the power is off with a voltage tester, take a photo of the wiring, then move each wire to the same terminal on an identical new switch and connect the ground. If the wiring does not match what you expect, stop and call a licensed electrician.
- [How to Replace an Electrical Outlet](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/replace-outlet/): Turn off the breaker, prove the outlet is dead at both receptacles with a tester, photograph the wiring, and move each wire to the matching terminal on a new outlet of the same rating: black to brass, white to silver, bare to green. Stop and call an electrician if the wiring is different or damaged.
- [How to Reset a Tripped Circuit Breaker](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/reset-tripped-breaker/): Turn off or unplug what was running on the dead circuit, open the panel, and find the breaker sitting in the middle or off position. Push it fully to OFF, then back to ON. If it trips again right away or keeps tripping, stop and call an electrician.
- [How to Reset a Tripped GFCI Outlet](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/reset-tripped-gfci/): Unplug everything on the dead outlets, find the GFCI outlet with TEST and RESET buttons (it may be in another room, the garage, or outside), and press RESET firmly until it clicks. If it will not reset or trips again right away, leave it off and call an electrician.
- [How to Stop a Smoke Alarm From Chirping](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/smoke-alarm-chirping/): A single chirp every 30 to 60 seconds usually means a low battery: replace it with the type printed on the alarm and press TEST. If it keeps chirping with a new battery, or the alarm is 10 years past its manufacture date, replace the whole alarm.

## Walls and Tile
- [How to Fix Drywall Nail Pops](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/fix-drywall-nail-pops/): Press the drywall tight to the stud and drive a drywall screw about 1 1/2 inches above and below the popped nail, then set or remove the nail and cover everything with two or three thin coats of compound. Covering the pop alone will not last.
- [How to Patch a Large Hole in Drywall](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/patch-large-drywall-hole/): Cut the damage into a clean square, screw wood backing strips inside the opening, screw in a matching piece of drywall, then tape the seams and finish with three thin coats of joint compound before priming and painting.
- [How to Patch a Small Hole in Drywall](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/patch-small-drywall-hole/): Fill nail holes and dents with spackling or joint compound in two or three thin coats, sanding lightly between. For holes from about 1 1/2 to 6 inches, cover the hole with a self-adhesive metal or mesh patch first, then feather three thin coats of compound over it, prime and paint.
- [How to Recaulk a Bathtub or Shower](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/caulk-a-bathtub/): Remove all the old caulk, clean off residue and mildew, let the joint dry completely, then tape both sides, run a bead of kitchen and bath caulk, smooth it, pull the tape while wet, and let it cure for about 24 hours before using the tub.
- [How to Regrout Tile](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/regrout-tile/): Scrape out the damaged grout with a grout saw or oscillating tool to about 1/8 inch deep, vacuum and dampen the joints, press new grout in diagonally with a rubber float, wipe the haze with a damp sponge, and let it cure before caulking corners or sealing.

## Doors and Windows
- [How to Fix a Door That Sticks](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/fix-sticking-door/): Find where the door rubs, then tighten the hinge screws, especially the top hinge; a longer screw into the framing often pulls a sagging door back square. Only if that fails, plane or sand the tight edge and seal the bare wood with primer and paint.
- [How to Fix a Door That Won't Latch](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/fix-door-wont-latch/): Find where the latch hits the strike plate (a little lipstick or chalk on the latch shows it), tighten the hinge screws, then file the strike opening a little larger or move the strike plate to line up. A longer screw in the top or bottom hinge can raise or lower the door.
- [How to Fix a Squeaky Door Hinge](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/fix-squeaky-door/): Tighten the hinge screws first, then tap out each hinge pin one at a time, clean it, and coat it with a light multipurpose oil or a dry graphite lubricant before tapping it back in. If a screw spins without tightening, fill the hole with glued wood slivers and redrive it.
- [How to Replace a Window Screen](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/replace-window-screen/): Pop out the old rubber spline, lay new screen mesh over the frame, and press it into the channel with a spline roller and new spline, working around the frame while keeping the mesh taut. Trim the excess with a utility knife.
- [How to Weatherstrip an Exterior Door](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/weatherstrip-door/): Close the door on a sheet of paper or look for daylight to find gaps, then replace worn weatherstripping on the jamb with a matching compression or kerf-in seal and add or adjust a door sweep at the bottom. The door should close with light resistance and no daylight showing.

## Appliances
- [Dishwasher Not Draining? How to Fix It](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/dishwasher-not-draining/): Check the sink side first: run the garbage disposal, clean the air gap cap if you have one, and look for a kinked drain hose. Then pull and rinse the filter in the bottom of the tub. On a newly installed dishwasher, the disposal's knockout plug may still be in place.
- [How to Clean a Dryer Vent](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/clean-dryer-vent/): Unplug the dryer (and shut off gas at the dryer's valve for a gas dryer), pull it out, disconnect the duct, and run a dryer vent brush through the duct and the wall vent to the outdoor hood. Vacuum the lint trap housing, reconnect with rigid or semi-rigid metal duct, and check that the outside flap opens when the dryer runs.
- [How to Fix a Jammed Garbage Disposal](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/fix-garbage-disposal-jam/): Turn the disposal switch off (unplug it or shut the breaker if you can), insert the 1/4 inch hex wrench into the socket in the center of the bottom of the unit, and work it back and forth until it turns freely. Remove the loosened object with tongs, let the motor cool, press the red reset button on the bottom, and test with cold water running.
- [Refrigerator Not Cooling? What to Check](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/fridge-not-cooling/): Check that the temperature controls are set correctly and the cooling is not switched off or in demo mode, make sure vents inside are not blocked by food, check the door seals, and clean dusty condenser coils with the fridge unplugged. If those checks do not help, a fan, compressor or control likely needs a technician.

## Outdoor
- [How to Clean Gutters Safely](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/clean-gutters/): Set an extension ladder on firm, level ground with a stabilizer so it rests on the roof rather than the gutter, scoop debris into a bucket starting near the downspouts, then flush the gutters and downspouts with a garden hose. Clean at least twice a year, more often under trees.
- [How to Fix a Leaky Outdoor Faucet (Hose Bib)](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/fix-leaky-outdoor-faucet/): If water leaks around the handle, tighten the packing nut behind the handle a quarter turn. If the spout drips with the handle closed, shut off the water to the spigot, unscrew the stem, and replace the rubber washer on the end. A spigot that leaks inside the wall after a freeze needs a pro.
- [How to Winterize Outdoor Faucets and Prevent Frozen Pipes](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/guides/winterize-outdoor-faucet/): Before the first hard freeze, disconnect and drain hoses, close the indoor shutoff valve for each outdoor faucet, then open the outdoor faucet to drain and leave it open. Add an insulated faucet cover. Keep the house heated to at least 55 degrees F when you are away.

## Calculators
- [Paint Coverage Calculator](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/calculators/paint-coverage/): Free paint calculator: enter room size, doors, windows and coats to estimate how many gallons of wall paint you need.
- [Tile and Flooring Calculator](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/calculators/tile-flooring/): Free flooring calculator: get square footage, waste allowance and the number of boxes of tile, laminate or vinyl plank to buy.
- [Mulch and Gravel Calculator](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/calculators/mulch-gravel/): Free mulch and gravel calculator: convert bed size and depth into cubic yards, 2 cubic foot bags, and approximate tons of gravel.

## Other
- [Basic home toolkit](https://homerepair.samcbarth.com/basic-home-toolkit/): A drill/driver, a screwdriver set, adjustable wrench, tongue-and-groove pliers, a tape measure, a utility knife, a non-contact voltage tester, a flange plunger, putty knives, a level, a stepladder and a flashlight cover most of the repairs on this site. Buy those first and add specialty tools as jobs come up.
